disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction of closed-period actuals is mechanical and automatable, but the council converged that automation must verify lock status rather than assume it (KB-03) and must provide a first-class manual-submission path for entities without automated lock signals, not a silent gap. It merges into TS-01 alongside comparatives loading because both are data-movement acts sharing one trigger and governance cadence.

Loading budget and forecast comparatives is a data-join with a genuine ambiguity point (which forecast is 'latest'); the council agreed this requires a stated deterministic tie-break algorithm and an explicit version identifier carried downstream, resolved as an exception only when the rule cannot decide. It shares TS-01's data-assembly lifecycle with VAR-01.

PVM/FX computation is deterministic once methodology is fixed, but the council (accounting_standards, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, finance_domain) converged that the methodology itself is a policy choice under KB-06 requiring versioned, approved governance distinct from data assembly, and that the FX effect must remain separately visible per KB-07/KB-08 rather than netted away. This is a distinct governed computation step, not a data-join, hence restructured rather than merely merged.

The mechanical threshold test is automated, satisfying VAR-R-08's survival requirement, but the council resolved the live conflict over per-cycle human involvement in favor of hitl_designer/finance_domain/emerging_economy: a standing, per-cycle, reason-coded override surface is retained because it is where genuine analyst pattern-recognition judgment is exercised, not merely periodic parameter governance. Structural and access-control separation from TS-06 satisfies VAR-R-04.

Budget holder commentary remains structurally unchanged in actor and accountability, as the council agreed against treating AI-assisted drafting as license to collapse confirmation into a frictionless click. AI drafting is retained only as a bounded, optional, distinguishable tool, with an escalation ladder and a low-tech equivalent affirmation path so accountability travels regardless of infrastructure.

Mechanical consolidation is automatable, but the council required the tie-out/reconciliation control to become a hard, blocking gate rather than a cosmetic field, preserving the evidential link (KB-02 by analogy) between reported explanation and actual movement, with an equivalent manual control for entities lacking assembly tooling.

VAR-R-07 requires this function to survive, and the council's strongest convergence (hitl_designer, accounting_standards, agentic_architect, finance_domain) was that review must not become lighter merely because arithmetic is guaranteed; instead it is re-engineered to see the judgment trail (methodology version, FX line, overrides, commentary affirmation status, tie-out resolutions) that automation would otherwise hide, making this a richer, not reduced, human step with the same actor as baseline.

Mechanical distribution is automated, but the council rejected auto-publish triggered directly by review approval: approval and release are kept as distinct, independently logged events so a correct, reviewed report can still be deliberately held, and distribution includes a document-based fallback for recipients without reliable dashboard access.

steps.actor: Data Assembly Agent (system); FP&A analyst as named exception owner and manual-adapter operator for legacy entities
steps.description: A Data Assembly Agent extracts actuals from the closed period and loads the approved budget version and latest forecast as comparatives, running as a scheduled/event-triggered pipeline against the consolidation and planning systems. The agent verifies an explicit per-entity lock-confirmation signal before extraction (it does not merely compare timestamps or assume closure), and resolves 'latest forecast' via a deterministic tie-breaking rule (highest version with approved status as of a cutoff timestamp), capturing budget and forecast version identifiers in its output. Entities on legacy or spreadsheet-based ledgers feed the same validated output schema through a defined manual-submission adapter populated by an FP&A analyst, rather than being silently excluded from automation. Any failure of the lock-verification gate, any version-ambiguity the tie-break rule cannot resolve, or any manual-adapter validation failure is routed as a named, triggered exception to the FP&A analyst's queue for resolution and logging; absent a defined exception, no person reviews the load.
steps.name: Automated actuals and comparatives assembly
outputs: Comparatives dataset (with budget and forecast version identifiers)
Exception queue entries (lock mismatch, version ambiguity, adapter validation failure)

steps.actor: Variance Computation Agent (system); Methodology Owner (FP&A manager or controller) approves methodology and rate-table versions
steps.description: A Variance Computation Agent, architecturally and lifecycle-separated from data assembly, computes price, volume and mix variances deterministically against a versioned, dated, approved methodology object (the sequencing convention and mix allocation basis) and a versioned constant-currency exchange-rate table. The engine never reads mutable, unapproved configuration: any change to the sequencing convention, allocation basis, or FX source triggers a re-approval workflow owned by a methodology owner (FP&A manager or controller) before the new version becomes active, and every variance record it produces carries the methodology-version tag that generated it. The isolated FX effect is retained as a separately identifiable line in the output dataset at every downstream stage — it is never netted into volume or mix for presentational convenience.
inputs: Accounting policies applied to actuals (as a versioned, approved methodology object)
steps.name: Governed variance computation with versioned methodology
outputs: Variance dataset (methodology-version tagged, FX effect as a separate line)
Methodology version history and approval events

steps.actor: Threshold & Triage system (rule engine); FP&A analyst (override exerciser); Threshold Parameter Owner (role access-control-separated from the TS-06 reviewer)
steps.description: A Threshold & Triage function, access-control-separated from both computation and review, applies a tiered, documented percentage-or-absolute materiality rules table mechanically to the variance dataset every cycle, selecting variances to explain. A standing, per-cycle override surface remains available to a named FP&A analyst to include a sub-threshold item (e.g., a flagged near-miss or watch-list driver) or exclude a borderline one; every override requires a mandatory reason code, is attributable to the individual who exercised it, and is logged immutably and made visible to the downstream reviewer. The identity permitted to edit the threshold rules table or exercise overrides is technically prevented — via role-based access control, periodically audited by a named owner — from also holding the review role in TS-06, enforcing the required actor separation structurally rather than by policy alone. The threshold table itself is periodically re-approved by a parameter owner distinct from the TS-06 reviewer.
inputs: Materiality thresholds (tiered percentage and absolute table, versioned)
steps.name: Automated threshold triage with accountable override

steps.description: Budget holders remain the accountable narrators of variance explanations; the step's structure, actor, and accountability are unchanged from baseline. An optional AI drafting assistant may generate a candidate explanation on request, but the state transition from draft to submitted commentary requires a human-originated edit-or-affirm action; the system logs whether commentary was edited, affirmed-as-is, or independently authored, and this draft/affirmed status travels with the commentary to review. For budget holders without reliable system access, a signed and dated paper/plain-template field is a co-equal, non-degraded mechanism for the same affirmation, not a lesser fallback. A defined escalation ladder (reminder, then manager/FP&A escalation, then a logged 'commentary pending' flag) handles non-response, explicitly accounting for connectivity and time-zone lag rather than assuming uniform responsiveness.
inputs: Plain commentary template / signed-and-dated field (low-tech equivalent)
steps.name: Obtain accountable commentary from budget holders
outputs: Budget holder commentary (tagged draft-affirmed, edited, or authored)
Escalation log for late or missing commentary

steps.actor: Report Assembly Agent (system); FP&A analyst resolves tie-out exceptions or performs manual assembly where unautomated
steps.description: A Report Assembly Agent consolidates the selected variances and budget holder commentary (confirmed or flagged-pending) into the draft report template. Before handoff to review, it runs a tie-out assertion that the sum of explained variances reconciles to the total reported movement within a defined tolerance; a failed tie-out is a blocking exception, not a cosmetic field, and the report cannot advance until a named analyst resolves it, logging what was missing, duplicated, or corrected. Where no assembly tooling exists, an analyst performs the same tie-out check manually as a mandatory, named sub-task, applying the identical pass/fail control logic.
steps.name: Automated report assembly with blocking tie-out control
outputs: Tie-out assertion result (pass or blocking exception)

steps.description: The FP&A manager reviews and challenges the draft report, retaining full authority to send commentary back to budget holders. Arithmetic re-derivation is not required since computation is deterministic and guaranteed upstream, but review depth and effort do not shrink: the reviewer's workspace surfaces, per variance line, the methodology version used, the isolated FX effect, any threshold override and its reason code, whether commentary was AI-drafted-and-affirmed-without-edit versus human-authored or edited, and how any tie-out exception was resolved. Review substance concentrates on narrative plausibility, cross-checks against information the automation cannot see, and scrutiny of where upstream judgment was exercised or thin.
inputs: Methodology version tag and FX effect line
steps.name: Review and challenge with judgment-trail visibility

steps.description: Review approval (TS-06) and release are distinct, independently logged events: approval changes the report's status, but a separate, deliberate release action by the FP&A manager triggers a Distribution Agent that formats and publishes the report, generating a document-based (e.g., PDF) fallback for any recipient without reliable dashboard access rather than assuming universal connectivity. The release screen presents an informed change-summary (new overrides, exceptions resolved since last cycle, count of unconfirmed commentary) so release is a deliberate, informed act rather than a formality indistinguishable from auto-publish.
steps.name: Manager release gate and distribution
outputs: Distributed variance report (dashboard and document-based formats)
